summary: Hermann Kulke is a historian and Indologist who studied at Freiburg under Ulrich Schneider, Madras, and Heidelberg, also studying under Hermann Goetz. He served as professor at Heidelberg (1967–1988) and Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Specializing in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, Hermann Lommel studied in Munich and Göttingen under Jacob Wackernagel, Friedrich Carl Andreas, and Hermann Oldenberg. He taught at Göttingen and was ordinary professor at Frankfurt (1920–1950).

Hermann Mittelberger, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. He held positions at Vienna, Utrecht, and Würzburg before serving as ordinary professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics at Graz (1971–2003).

Linguist Hermann Møller studied at Kiel, Leipzig (under Georg Curtius; Ph.D.), Munich, Berlin, and Breslau. He held Privatdozent appointments at Kiel University (1878) and the University of Copenhagen (1883).

Active in Indology and music theory, Hermann Oesterley studied at Leipzig and earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen. He served as Privatdozent at Kiel, worked at Göttingen State and University Library, and was Kustos at Wrocław University Library (1873–1891).

A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Hermann Oldenberg studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He served as a Privatdozent in Berlin, Ordinarius at Kiel (1889–1908), and professor at Göttingen from 1908.

Religious studies scholar Hermann Olshausen studied at Kiel and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts in Berlin, served as professor of Protestant theology at Königsberg (1827–1834), and taught at Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

A linguist and Indologist, Hermann Osthoff studied in Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Bonn under Johann Gildemeister and Hermann Usener, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Leipzig. He was Privatdozent at Leipzig and professor and director at Heidelberg (1877; 1887).

Linguist Hermann Paul studied in Berlin under Heymann Steinthal and in Leipzig under Friedrich Zarncke, Georg Curtius, and August Leskien. He served as professor at Freiburg (1874–1893) and professor of German philology at Munich (1893–1916).

A scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology, Hermann Sauppe studied under Bernhard Hirzel and completed a doctorate at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He held posts at Zurich, Zentralbibliothek Zürich, Weimar, and the University of Göttingen (from 1855).

Hermann Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Munich and taught at Humboldt University of Berlin (1851).

A scholar of religious studies and linguistics, Hermann Usener studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and University of Bonn (~1866–1905).
Hermann Walter studied Indology at Neuchâtel, Edinburgh, Tübingen, and Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as lecturer and professor of Modern and Germanic Languages at McGill University (1900–1936).
Indologist Hermann Weller studied at the University of Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He later returned to Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent (1930) and honorary professor (1938–1952).

Linguist Hermann Wilhelm Ebel studied under August Friedrich Pott at Halle and August Boeckh and Franz Bopp at Berlin. After teaching at secondary schools, he succeeded Bopp as professor of comparative philology at Berlin in 1872.
Hertha Krick was an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Gerhard Oberhammer. She subsequently worked as an assistant at the University of Vienna from 1972 until 1979.

Hervey DeWitt Griswold worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Union College, Union Theological Seminary, Oxford, Berlin, and Cornell. He was professor of philosophy at Forman Christian College (1894–1914) and visiting lecturer at Columbia (1923–1929).

Hew McLeod was a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Nelson College, the University of Otago, and SOAS University of London, and later served on the editorial board at Otago (attested 2005).

Heymann Steinthal worked in linguistics and philosophy, studying under August Boeckh at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held long-term posts at Berlin (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and was attested as a researcher there in 1995.
